clue.text: Criminal gang has it

blocks.note: a band is a group or gang
taken as written

explanation.surface: A criminal gang is said to have possession of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is an outlaw or robber, so the noun is a synonym for a criminal.

clue.text: Voice ready to break bursting aloft

indicators.note: something bursting flies apart, so the word after it is broken up and rearranged
one word breaking into another splits it and sits in the gap

blocks.note: set means prepared or ready, as in 'ready, steady, go'
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer's voice, about to crack, soars up high.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of aloft are rearranged and split by the word for ready.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsetto is the artificially high register of a male singer, a kind of voice.

clue.text: Opener once in abstract game

blocks.note: to draw out is to abstract or extract
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: An opening move once seen in some abstract board game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' suggests a chess opening; it is the lowering bridge that opened a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawbridge was the hinged bridge lowered to open access across a castle moat, so it served as an opener in former times.

clue.text: Tie with netting, marked green

blocks.note: netting a goal is scoring, and a marked surface is scored
green and raw both mean inexperienced or unripe

explanation.surface: A tie wrapped in netting, with a green mark on it.
explanation.walkthrough: In football (soccer) a score draw is a drawn match in which both sides scored, as opposed to a goalless draw.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is a drawn match, and a score draw is a particular kind of drawn result.

clue.text: Steering apparatus in hard wood

blocks.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
elm is a kind of tree and its timber

explanation.surface: A ship's steering gear made of a hard wood.
explanation.definitionFit: The helm is the tiller or wheel by which a vessel is steered.

clue.text: Old Germanic character in outer parts of Burundi, small country

indicators.note: the outer parts of a word are its first and last letters only
one thing in another sits inside it, here between two letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of the word
runes were the letters of early Germanic alphabets

explanation.surface: An ancient script found on the borders of Burundi, a small African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Burundi is itself a small country, tempting the solver to take it as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a tiny sultanate on the island of Borneo, one of the smallest states in Asia.

clue.text: Castle geared toward getting lock

blocks.note: something geared toward a purpose is for it
a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: A castle designed to get a secure lock on its gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortress is a fortified stronghold, much as a castle is.

clue.text: Plane to Nepal, for instance?

blocks.note: surface reading: a flight to the Himalayan kingdom
setter's reading: turning the five letters of the first word into the second is an example of a familiar word game

explanation.surface: An example of an aircraft heading for Kathmandu.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of plane rearranged spell nepal, so the change of one word into the other is the thing being exemplified.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed by rearranging another's letters, as plane becomes nepal, is the very device crosswords use most.

clue.text: Baby power, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: the phrase asks us to listen to a word rather than read its spelling

blocks.note: might is power or strength

explanation.surface: Infant strength, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: Baby is the definition, used as an adjective-like noun for a tiny child.
explanation.definitionFit: A mite is a small child, a little one, so the word stands for a baby.

clue.text: All the best English port taken by revolutionary

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the archetypal revolutionary
E is the abbreviation for English
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A farewell wish as an English port is seized by a rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is an informal British goodbye, used in the same spirit as signing off with good wishes.

clue.text: Holding back of plate, wash dirt off — in this?

definitions.text: Holding back of plate, wash dirt off — in this?

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter
something gone off is spoiled, so these letters are put out of order
holding something means keeping it within, so one letter goes inside the rest

blocks.note: the final letter
taken as written, to be rearranged around the single letter

explanation.surface: Scrub the grime off a plate, and ask what liquid it goes into.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: wordplay, then a picture of the water you clean crockery in.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishwater is the water used for washing up plates and cutlery, the liquid you would clean dirt off a plate in.

clue.text: French painter returning mid-morning?

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: ten o'clock in the morning is a fair time for mid-morning

explanation.surface: A French artist coming back home at mid-morning.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-morning is written as a clock time, ten am, and then turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet was a nineteenth-century French painter, forerunner of Impressionism.

clue.text: Rubbish queen for King Edward, say

blocks.note: tat is cheap junk
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: Trading a worthless queen for a king, as in some card game.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a popular British potato variety, not a monarch; tater is slang for potato.
explanation.definitionFit: A tater is a colloquial potato, and the King Edward is a well-known example of a potato variety.

clue.text: Drop in business after Christmas time

indicators.note: one part coming after another is placed to its right in the answer

blocks.note: DEC is the calendar abbreviation for December
one's line is one's trade or business

explanation.surface: Trade falls off once the Christmas rush is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about a post-holiday slump; 'Drop' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline is to fall or sink, so as a verb it is a synonym of drop.

clue.text: Boot, one going on one foot: some earth on top

indicators.note: in a down answer, what goes on top is written first

blocks.note: a clod is a lump of earth
someone who hops moves on one foot

explanation.surface: A boot, worn by someone hopping, caked in mud on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A clodhopper is a large heavy shoe or boot, a humorous name for clumsy footwear.

clue.text: Kids on holiday before April or May, say?

blocks.note: someone off work is on holiday
both months fall in the spring season

explanation.surface: Children going on holiday ahead of the spring months.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are a person's children, so the word is a synonym for kids.

clue.text: Hanger-on in class doomed, for failing to grasp minimum of workings

indicators.note: the least part of a word is taken to be just its opening letter
a failing thing breaks down, so the words are reduced to letters and rearranged
grasping something means holding it within, so a letter goes inside the rest

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A doomed class failing for lack of even the slightest working shown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanger-on' looks like a sycophant, but here it is literally something that hangs over a person.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Greek legend a sword hung by a single hair over Damocles' head, so it is a thing hanging on above someone, an ever-present peril.

clue.text: After period of time, man is giving punishment

indicators.note: one part following another is written to its right in the answer

blocks.note: a span is a stretch of time
a king is a piece, or man, in chess

explanation.surface: After a while, a man starts handing out discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: A chess piece is called a man, so man can give KING.
explanation.definitionFit: A spanking is a smacking on the bottom, a form of physical punishment.

clue.text: Sweet loaf, one with lemonade?

blocks.note: to loaf about is to loll or laze
I is the Roman numeral for one
pop is fizzy soft drink

explanation.surface: A sweet bread roll served with a fizzy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaf' looks like a noun, a lump of bread, but it is the verb meaning to laze.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a hard sweet on a stick, a piece of confectionery.

clue.text: Player reacts when beaten by striker's header

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked out of shape, so the word is rearranged
a word's header is what heads it, its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A footballer reacts when outdone by the centre forward's headed goal.
explanation.walkthrough: Player, striker and header all suggest football, but the player is a stage performer.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress is a female performer in plays, and player is an old word for an actor.

clue.text: Cast dumbfounded

blocks.note: first meaning: hurled, past participle of a verb for tossing
second meaning: confused or disconcerted, as when someone is put off their stride

explanation.walkthrough: Cast suggests actors who are speechless, but it is simply the past participle of a verb for hurling.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrown is both the past participle of throw, as cast is, and an informal adjective for disconcerted or bewildered.

clue.text: Room to eat a Muslim burger, say?

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing such a burger

indicators.note: something that eats another takes it inside itself

blocks.note: a hall is a large room
taken as written

explanation.surface: A place where Muslims can go for a burger.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer describes a burger prepared according to Islamic law.
explanation.definitionFit: Halal food is meat slaughtered and prepared as Islamic law permits, so a Muslim's burger would typically be of this kind.

clue.text: Bank perhaps fine not opening?

indicators.note: without its opening, a word loses its first letter

blocks.note: fine and slender both mean thin

explanation.surface: Might a bank be fine without opening its doors?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not opening' looks like a bank shut for business, but it removes a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank is an example of a lender, an institution that loans money.

clue.text: Red spots in green cabbage coming up

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning them
in a down answer, coming up means read from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Red blemishes appearing on a green cabbage leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition producing red pimples, so it is a collective name for spots.

clue.text: Curry scoffed by Mick or Mark

indicators.note: something scoffed has been swallowed, so the answer is inside the words that follow

blocks.note: letters spanning the words

explanation.surface: A curry wolfed down by one of two friends, Mick or Mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A korma is a mild, creamy Indian dish, one type of curry.

clue.text: Scrap the first thirteen letters

blocks.note: the alphabet's first thirteen run from the first letter to the thirteenth

explanation.surface: Throw out the opening thirteen letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrap looks like a verb for discarding, but it is a noun; the run of letters is read as 'A to M'.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the tiniest particle, so the word means a scrap or the smallest bit of something.

clue.text: Party piece not bad after fourth of sherries

indicators.note: the fourth of a word means its fourth letter only
something bad has gone wrong, so the words before it are put into disorder
one part coming after another is written to its right in the answer

blocks.note: the fourth letter
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A party trick that's quite decent once you've had a few sherries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party piece' and 'not bad' read as fixed phrases; split them, with 'Party' the definition and 'not' part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A reception is a formal social gathering, such as after a wedding, so it is a kind of party.

clue.text: Night light women switched on

indicators.note: things switched around change places, so the word's letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lamp for the night that some women turned on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switched on' reads as one phrase for a lamp; 'on' is in fact kept as written.
explanation.definitionFit: The new moon is a phase of the moon, the body that lights the night sky.

clue.text: Vision of ugliness viewed by me, reportedly?

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by speech not spelling

blocks.note: what was viewed by me is what I saw

explanation.surface: Something hideous that I happened to see.
explanation.walkthrough: In British non-rhotic speech the final R is silent, so the phrase for what I viewed sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something very ugly to look at, an unsightly thing.
